definitions.ttfbMs: Time from sending the request until the first response headers arrive. For a page that redirects, this is the redirect, not the HTML.
definitions.totalMs: Time from sending the request until the final response body ends. Page redirects are included.
definitions.bytes: Bytes received on the wire. The client does not decompress them.
definitions.contentEncoding: The content-encoding header on the response, or identity when that header is absent.
definitions.byteMatch: stored-br, stored-gz, or raw when the wire size equals that file. other when it equals none of them. null for routes that are not wasm.
definitions.cold: The first request to that route in this process. Only page-home is the first request after wrangler dev becomes ready.
definitions.steady: Five requests after one discarded warm-up. The median is the middle sample.
definitions.pageCount: A 200 HTML response from the Worker schedules countPageView. The script then reads local D1 and requires that rise on routes whose final path is the path it requested. A redirect onto a path outside run_worker_first is stored and not required. There is no public route that reads the counts.
definitions.authEnv: wrangler dev receives a generated BETTER_AUTH_SECRET through --env-file. .dev.vars is not read. Commentary, Paddle, and sign-in keys are unset.

productionBlindSpots: The clock is local wrangler dev, which is miniflare on this machine. It is not the Cloudflare edge and it has no edge cache.
Cloudflare replaces the browser Accept-Encoding with br, gzip before the Worker runs. The browser header is request.cf.clientAcceptEncoding. Local wrangler does not do that replacement.
Miniflare can recompress a Worker response. When gzip is listed before br, a body the Worker stored as Brotli can arrive as gzip. cache-control no-transform does not stop that in local dev.
Page-count inserts run in waitUntil after the response. totalMs ends when the body ends.
